newsitem.title: USA: Talks on saving California redwoods to resume.
newsitem.headline: Talks on saving California redwoods to resume.

text.p: Talks aimed at stopping loggers from cutting thousands of acres of ancient redwoods in northern California will resume later this week, a spokeswoman for Sen. Dianne Feinstein said Tuesday.
The government wants to exchange areas of virgin redwoods in the nation's largest privately owned redwood forest for surplus federal land or rights to harvest trees on other federal land.

The nearly 200,000 acres of private forest is held by Pacific Lumber Co, a unit of Maxxam Inc. Texas financier Charles Hurwitz, chairman of Maxxam, had pledged a two-week moratorium on cutting trees in the 3,000-acre Headwaters area, home to endangered fish and birds. That moratorium ends Monday.
Feinstein, Deputy Interior Secretary John Garamendi and California State Resources Secretary Doug Wheeler will meet Hurwitz Thursday in the California Democrat's office, a spokeswoman there said.
At issue has been how much acreage should be saved and how Maxxam will be compensated.
Environmentalists want a 60,000-acre area saved, contending it is necessary to preserve the ecosystem. But negotiations have focused on much smaller areas.

The company says the Headwaters grove and its buffer area is about 4,500 acres. In addition, Feinstein said, "there's some other little areas in there with ancient forests that are called the lesser cathdrals."
A spokesman for Maxxam in Houston said those other areas amount to 1,800 acres and are also included in the moratorium.
The struggle between environmentalists and the company sparked one of the largest one-day mass arrests in California history earlier this month, with 897 people arrested and booked.
